subject: Next steps: keying model options and scope for NoblePay PII flows

Subject: Next steps: keying model options and scope for NoblePay PII flows

Hi Tim / Elena,

Thanks again for carving out time today — appreciated the detailed walk-through of NoblePay's card-processing PII flows. Per the demo and security call, I've summarized the realistic keying approaches we discussed and proposed next steps so your security and engineering teams have a crisp path to evaluate.

Summary of options we discussed (high level):
- Redwood-managed keys (default): platform holds CMKs; we provide audit logs and rotation cadence. Fastest to go-live, minimal ops for NoblePay.
- Customer-managed keys (BYOK via KMS): NoblePay retains CMKs in their cloud KMS/HSM and provides an integration token. We support wrapped-key upload + automated key rotation compatibility.
- HSM-attested custody (customer HSM): NoblePay owns HSM and we integrate via approved KMIP/Cloud-HSM connectors. Best for regulatory control; longer onboarding and procurement.

Info we need from you to qualify a recommended path:
1) Which workloads must be under customer key control? (e.g., tokenization shard, embeddings, full text logs)
2) Required retention window for request/response logs containing PII (we noted 30/90/365-day possibilities)
3) Any blocking regulatory requirement to keep keys on-prem or in specific cloud region
4) Who will own key rotation policy and who needs access to key material for forensics

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Technical deep-dive (45m) with Karthik (security eng) and Vanessa (SE) to map NoblePay flows to the integration patterns. Options: Thu 5/23 10:00am PT or Fri 5/24 11:00am PT.
- I attached a short matrix (redwood_kms-options.pdf) that maps feature trade-offs by option.

Please confirm preferred deep-dive slot and share the answers to the 4 bullets above when you get a chance. If your procurement team needs a minimal SOW for BYOK onboarding, Monica (cc) can start a draft.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0162

Attachments: redwood_kms-options.pdf (summary), encryption_matrix_v2.xlsx (detailed tradeoffs)
From: Tim Jansen <tim.jansen@noblepay.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@noblepay.com>, NoblePay Security <secops@noblepay.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 11:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: keying model options and scope for NoblePay PII flows

Priyom — thanks for the note and the clear matrix, that helps. Quick answers to your bullets so you have context ahead of the deep-dive:  

1) Mandatory BYOK scope: anything that would allow reconstruction of full PAN or unmasked PII. At minimum we need tokenization keys and any intermediate embeddings that might be reversible. Non-sensitive analytics (aggregated metrics) can use Redwood-managed keys.
2) Retention: security policy prefers 90 days for request logs, with capability to put specific sessions into longer-term forensic retention (up to 2 years) on a per-case basis. We need sampling controls on logging.
3) Residency: keys for EU customers must remain in EU (we have a small EU footprint). For US card flows, cloud KMS is acceptable but keys must be under our control (BYOK).
4) Ownership: NoblePay will own rotation policy; we will want API hooks/audit trails for rotation events and access.

We can do Thu 5/23 10:00am PT for the technical session. I will have our lead security engineer, Elena Ruiz, and one of our infra engineers join.

Two additional asks:
- Can you share any sample audit log output for key-use events (token decrypt/rotate) so our audit team can validate fields?
- Do you support dual-control approval for key import/rotation (i.e., two-person approval flows)?

Tim
Tim Jansen
Security Lead, NoblePay

Thanks Tim — great clarity, that helps a lot. Confirmed for Thu 5/23 10:00am PT.

Quick replies to your two asks:
- Audit log sample: attaching a redwood_key-usage-log-sample.txt (see attached stub in PDF pack). The sample includes timestamped events for key-wrap/unwrap, token-decrypt, and admin operations with actor id, request-id, and event outcome.
- Dual-control: Redwood supports delegated approval workflows for key import and HSM onboarding via our integration layer. We can model a two-approver gate by wiring a short approval webhook into your ticketing system (we generally recommend Okta/ServiceNow connector). We'll cover an implementation sketch in the deep-dive.

Prep for the technical deep-dive (what we'll cover in the 45m):
- Map of NoblePay PII paths -> suggested keying model (BYOK for tokenization + optional customer HSM for highest assurance)
- Demo of audit logs and rotation events (Karthik)
- Network/residency controls: region pinning, egress minimization
- Rollout plan + minimal SOW + expected timeline (Monica)

Vanessa — can you own a 10-slide tech-sketch that we can walk through (I'll share here). Monica — we'll draft a short SOW after the deep-dive.

See you on the call,
Priyom
